# Education — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Other Education: typically around 650, most listings 230-3,900 (37 listings)
- Textbooks: typically around 400, most listings 200-800 (25 listings)
- Courses: typically around 800, most listings 50-55,000 (11 listings — thin data and a legitimately huge spread, from trial classes to full course fees; lean on general judgment)

This is mostly a low-value category (used books, handwritten notes, stationery, study furniture). Prices of Rs 50-200 for notes or secondhand textbooks are normal — do NOT treat a low price alone as a scam signal here. The scam-price heuristic for high-value goods barely applies; only a high-priced course with vague or too-good claims warrants extra scrutiny.

## What good listings look like
- "clamphook IOE entrance preparation books" — Rs 3,000
- "class 10 vedenta book" — Rs 250
- "physics chapter 1 basic notes of 'UNITS AND DIMENSIONS'" — Rs 100
- "Foundation of mathamtices class XI" — Rs 600
- "Study Table for Students" — Rs 999

A good listing names the subject plus the class/level in the Nepali system (class 8-12, +2, SEE, or entrance exams like IOE/CEE/BLE), and for books the publisher or edition and condition. Minor spelling errors are common and fine.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Study-abroad or visa-consultancy style pitches promising guaranteed visas, scholarships, or overseas job placement — a well-known consultancy scam pattern in Nepal; hold.
- Offers to sell actual/leaked exam question papers (SEE, +2, entrance), guaranteed-pass schemes, or ready-made degrees/certificates without study; hold.
- Clearly non-education items posted here (e.g. a collectible "Nepali ancient currency" appeared in this category's samples) — obvious wrong-category posts should hold for recategorization.
